clue.text: No longer looking after someone for nothing?

definitions.meaning: having been relieved of a ward or dependant in one's care, with no one left to mind

explanation.surface: A carer who has just stopped looking after someone wonders whether they did it unpaid.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes 'charge' as a person in your care: to be free of that charge is to have no one left to look after.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses rest on 'charge': a ward you are responsible for, and a price asked; being free of either fits.

clue.text: Pull back engineers' handle

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps
to treat something is to handle or deal with it

explanation.surface: An instruction to yank back a lever on the engineers' machine.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat is to withdraw, as an army pulls back from a position.

clue.text: Former Italian banker guaranteed public appearance

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
the Po is Italy's longest river, and a river is a 'banker' because it has banks
sure means certain or guaranteed

explanation.surface: A one-time Italian financier is assured of being seen in public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' suggests finance, but in crosswords it is often a river, something with banks; here the Italian river Po.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposure is being put on show in public, such as media coverage or appearing before an audience.

clue.text: Flying firm

definitions.meaning: fixed ..., as a door stuck ... or colours that will not run

explanation.definitionFit: Speedy for the first sense; securely fixed and immovable for the second.

clue.text: Superior holds bag for Scotsman

indicators.note: the first word holding the second places the second inside it

parts.note: superior means higher in rank or position
to bag a fish or a prize is to land it

explanation.surface: A senior official has a bag set aside for a man from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bag' reads as a sack; here it is the verb, as an angler bags or lands a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highlander is a native of the Scottish Highlands, a mountainous northern region of Scotland.

clue.text: We're moving around noon, to begin again

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the next piece
the letters of the word are on the move, so they are shuffled

explanation.surface: People announce that at midday they are relocating to make a fresh start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges WERE to RE-EW, and 'around' puts N between, giving RE-N-EW.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew something is to resume or restart it after a break.

clue.text: Few words to say about someone who is late?

definitions.text: Few words to say about someone who is late?

parts.words: Few words to say about someone who is late?
parts.note: reads like an excuse for a latecomer, but 'late' means dead: a short inscription about the deceased

explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' suggests someone who arrives after time; it means someone who has died, as in 'the late Mr Smith'.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is a brief inscription on a tomb or a short tribute in memory of a dead person.

clue.text: Founder with reason to hide

parts.note: to founder is to sink or fail, to go under
a ground is a reason or basis, as in grounds for complaint

explanation.surface: The man who started the company has a good reason to keep out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Founder' reads as a noun, someone who set something up; here it is the verb meaning to sink.
explanation.definitionFit: To go underground is to go into hiding, as a resistance fighter or fugitive does.

clue.text: Fulfils promise, giving reserves the same weapon

parts.note: to reserve something is to keep it back
one can mean the same or united, as in 'of one mind'
a sword is a bladed weapon

explanation.surface: Someone honours a pledge by handing their stand-ins identical arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the same' is the hard piece: 'one' carries that sense in phrases like 'of one mind', and the apostrophe in the answer is ignored when the pieces join.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep one's word is to do what one promised, honouring a pledge.

clue.text: Swimmer with 31 days work

parts.note: October has 31 days, abbreviated Oct
an opus is a work, especially a musical composition

explanation.surface: A competitive swimmer has put in a month's training.
explanation.walkthrough: Several months have 31 days, but only October gives a letter run that fits.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus is a sea creature that moves through the water, so it is a swimmer.

clue.text: Non-Jewish man on French island

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman, a man
île is French for island; 'on' places it after the first piece

explanation.surface: A Gentile man lives on an island off France.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentile is a person who is not Jewish, used here as an adjective.

clue.text: Requires name before distributing seed

indicators.note: the first piece is placed in front of the next one
the letters of the word are spread out and reordered

explanation.surface: A gardener's instructions call for a label before sowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributing' rearranges SEED to EEDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To need something is to require it, so needs and requires are synonyms.

clue.text: Strippers use it and shock US city member!

parts.note: a blow is a shock or setback
LA is Los Angeles
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Exotic dancers shock a politician from Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strippers' suggests exotic dancers; it means decorators who strip old paint with a flame.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowlamp is a torch whose hot flame softens old paint so decorators can scrape it off.

clue.text: Seat frame being of steel dread slipping

indicators.note: the letters slip out of place, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A frame made of steel is feared because it might slide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slipping' rearranges the ten letters of STEEL DREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddletree is the internal frame on which a horse's saddle is built.

clue.text: Go in satin dress, which amuses

parts.note: to enter is to go in

indicators.note: to dress is to arrange, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Arriving in a satin dress is something that delights onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress' looks like a garment but is the anagram signal, turning SATIN into TAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain people is to amuse them.

clue.text: Go away when mum rings

parts.note: mum means silent, and 'sh' is the call for silence
O is ring-shaped, so two rings are OO

explanation.surface: Someone is told to leave when their mother phones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like mother and 'rings' like phoning; they are silence (SH) and two circles (OO).
explanation.definitionFit: Shoo is said to drive an animal or person off, an order to leave.

clue.text: Quiet and still depressed

parts.note: calm means still or untroubled
down means low in spirits

explanation.surface: Someone is quiet, unmoving and feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quiet' is the verb here, to soothe, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To quiet someone is to soothe them until they settle.

clue.text: It's good to have something to wear

parts.note: to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: It is nice to have some clothes to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: A gown is a long dress or robe, a garment.

clue.text: Ready to fly out of trouble

indicators.note: the flying word sits outside the trouble word, wrapped around it

parts.note: to wing is to fly
ill means trouble or harm, as in ills of society

explanation.surface: A bird is prepared to take off and escape a difficult spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' reads as escaping; it puts WING outside ILL, giving W-ILL-ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Willing means prepared or ready to do something.

clue.text: Hormone replacement Adele ran in for

indicators.note: the letters are put back in a new order, a reordering of the words that follow

explanation.surface: In hormone replacement therapy, the singer Adele stepped in for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hormone replacement' looks like one phrase (as in HRT); 'replacement' is in fact the anagram signal for ADELE RAN IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenaline is the hormone released by the adrenal glands in response to stress.

clue.text: Stirring rice with tin stirrer?

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A cook mixes rice in a tin with a spoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirrer' is a cook's spoon in the picture; it means someone who stirs up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: An inciter provokes others to act, a troublemaker who stirs things up.

clue.text: Observer agreed upon appearance by Queen

indicators.note: the first piece is placed up against the next
next to: the last piece stands beside the rest

parts.note: 'you're on' means agreed, accepted
a look is an appearance
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone watching agrees about how the Queen looks.
explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker is a spectator who watches without taking part.

clue.text: Is to round up Elizabeth the basket-maker

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' reads the letters from the bottom upwards

parts.note: O is round in shape
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A woman named Elizabeth, who weaves baskets, is about to gather people in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns both 'Is' and 'round' together, as this is a down clue; the basket-maker is the willow that baskets are woven from, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Willow shoots are the flexible material woven into baskets, so they 'make' the basket.

clue.text: Calcium found in stomach of bird

indicators.note: the element is located inside the stomach word

parts.note: a maw is an animal's stomach or jaws
Ca is the chemical symbol for calcium

explanation.surface: Traces of calcium are found in a bird's gut.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaw is a large, brightly coloured parrot of tropical America.

clue.text: Part of one picture of impressive proportions

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of a single painting is on a grand scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic describes something heroic and huge in scale, like an epic film.

clue.text: One Iris Turner is more vociferous!

indicators.note: something that turns the letters round, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A woman called Iris who turns things is louder than the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' looks like a surname (or the painter); it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Vociferous means loud and clamorous, so the comparative is louder.

clue.text: University disciplinarian all for dropping a performer

parts.note: pro means in favour of, all for

indicators.note: dropping a letter means it is removed from the word

parts.note: an actor is a performer

explanation.surface: A university official is keen on sacking an actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping a' takes the A off ACTOR, leaving CTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford and Cambridge a proctor is an official responsible for student discipline.

clue.text: Anger centred on change of plant distribution area

indicators.note: a change of the letters means they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rage focused on altering how plants are dispersed around a region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of' rearranges ANGER CENTRED.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden centre is a shop selling plants and gardening supplies.
